fields.cs_content: How Maintain Technology Aligned Two Stalled Parties in Just 10 Days Using Its Contract Mediation Methodology
fields.cs_subtitle: A major transformation program had come to a standstill as two key delivery partners became embroiled in a dispute over contract terms, milestone payments, and scope interpretation. The relationship had deteriorated, deadlines were slipping, and both sides were preparing for a prolonged legal battle.

The Contract Mediation Methodology
Maintain Technology deployed its 4-phase rapid mediation framework, designed for high-stakes IT delivery disputes:
fields.cs_testimonial: “Maintain Technology brought clarity, neutrality, and speed. They helped us go from months of deadlock to a signed agreement in just 10 days — and got the program moving again.”

title: Piloted SAP IAM to Modernise Asset Management

fields.cs_title: Piloted SAP IAM to Modernise Asset Management
fields.cs_content: How Maintain Technology Used a Three-Horizon Approach to Optimise, Modernise, and Transform Asset Management
fields.cs_engagement: SAP Intelligent Asset Management (IAM) Proof of Concept
fields.cs_outcome: Clear transformation model established, blending ageing and modern technology to unlock the art of the possible.
fields.cs_subtitle: The client was struggling with poor asset performance that caused excessive downtime and high reactive maintenance costs, compounded by the absence of a clear technology roadmap to guide future investments. Multiple IT initiatives had failed due to misalignment between operational needs, existing legacy systems, and modern platforms.
fields.cs_challenge: The client was struggling with poor asset performance that caused excessive downtime and high reactive maintenance costs, compounded by the absence of a clear technology roadmap to guide future investments. Multiple IT initiatives had failed due to misalignment between operational needs, existing legacy systems, and modern platforms. As a result, the organisation was left with an environment of uncertainty, low stakeholder confidence, and no unified vision for how asset management should evolve.
fields.cs_testimonial: “Maintain Technology showed us what was possible — not just in the next quarter, but over the next five years. They helped us bridge our old systems with modern capabilities, and gave us a clear path to full transformation.”
fields.cs_why_it_matters: Many asset-intensive organisations are caught between ageing technology and the promise of digital transformation. Maintain Technology’s three-horizon approach ensures that optimisation starts today, modernisation is strategically phased, and transformation is achievable without unnecessary risk or cost.
fields.cs_approach_-_description_1: Maintain Technology applied its Optimise → Modernise → Transform model to structure the engagement and deliver both short-term wins and long-term vision:
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_1:
Analysed current asset management processes and technology stack. 

Identified efficiency improvements achievable with existing systems. 

Established baseline performance metrics to track improvement.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_2:
Designed a Proof of Concept (POC) using SAP Intelligent Asset Management to demonstrate “the art of the possible” by combining legacy systems with modern digital capabilities. 

Enabled predictive maintenance, centralised asset visibility, and mobile-enabled work management.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_3:
Created an enterprise-wide transformation blueprint aligning asset management practices to ISO 55000 standards. 

Defined a phased roadmap to replace ageing systems, standardise processes, and embed data-driven decision-making.
fields.cs_result_-_list_1: Proof of Concept Delivered — Validated that ageing systems could be enhanced with modern capabilities to deliver immediate business value.
fields.cs_result_-_list_2: Future Vision Agreed — Clear alignment on how to optimise, modernise, and ultimately transform asset management across the enterprise.
fields.cs_result_-_list_3: Performance Uplift — Early pilot results showed improved maintenance planning accuracy and asset performance tracking.

title: Cut Delivery Costs by 50% Through Offshore Transition

fields.cs_title: Cut Delivery Costs by 50% Through Offshore Transition
fields.cs_content: How Maintain Technology Optimised the Onshore–Offshore Model to Deliver Sustainable Cost Savings Without Compromising Performance
fields.cs_outcome: 50% reduction in delivery costs, maintained service targets, and a stable long-term onshore–offshore capability.
fields.cs_subtitle: The client was facing high project and application maintenance costs that consumed a significant portion of the budget and limited investment in innovation. Their delivery model was inefficient, heavily reliant on high-cost onshore resources, and previous attempts at offshoring had failed.
fields.cs_challenge: The client was facing high project and application maintenance costs that consumed a significant portion of the budget and limited investment in innovation. Their delivery model was inefficient, heavily reliant on high-cost onshore resources, and previous attempts at offshoring had failed—cost savings were negated by delivery issues, quality degradation, and missed targets. The leadership team therefore needed a solution that could reduce costs sustainably without repeating the mistakes of earlier offshore transitions.
fields.cs_testimonial: “We’d seen offshoring fail before. Maintain Technology made it work by getting the onshore–offshore model right from the start — aligning skills, governance, and culture.”
fields.cs_why_it_matters: Offshoring is not a cost-saving silver bullet — it can fail without the right model. Maintain Technology’s outsourcing methodology ensures cost efficiency is balanced with capability, quality, and long-term sustainability, turning offshoring from a risk into a competitive advantage.
fields.cs_approach_-_description_1: We deployed a structured, capability-first model to ensure offshoring worked in practice — not just on paper:
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_1:
Analysed service catalogue, cost structures, delivery performance, and skill distribution. 

Identified functions and activities most suited for offshore delivery without impacting service targets.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_2:
Matched offshore partner capabilities to client requirements, focusing on technical skills, domain knowledge, and service quality history. 

Defined clear roles and accountability split between onshore and offshore teams.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_3:
Designed governance and communication structures to bridge cultural and time-zone differences. 

Established joint KPIs to drive shared accountability. 

Embedded a “follow the sun” approach for faster turnaround and reduced downtime.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_4:
Piloted with a subset of services before scaling. 

Structured knowledge transfer sessions and shadow-support periods to safeguard quality.
fields.cs_result_-_list_1: 50% reduction in delivery costs across project and application maintenance functions.
fields.cs_result_-_list_2: No drop in performance — all SLA and KPI targets maintained during and after transition.
fields.cs_result_-_list_3: Sustainable onshore–offshore capability with embedded governance and continuous improvement processes.
fields.cs_result_-_list_4: Proven repeatable model for future offshoring without the pitfalls seen in prior attempts.

title: Improved Go-Live Quality with Assured Testing Standards

fields.cs_title: Improved Go-Live Quality with Assured Testing Standards
fields.cs_content: How Maintain Technology Reduced Defects and Increased Go-Live Confidence Through Structured Testing Assurance
fields.cs_outcome: Significant reduction in post-go-live defects, smoother cutovers, and improved stakeholder confidence.
fields.cs_subtitle: The client’s projects were plagued by poor quality assurance processes that resulted in high defect counts in production, stressful go-lives requiring emergency fixes, and extended post-implementation support. With no consistent testing methodology in place, quality standards varied widely between vendors and teams.
fields.cs_challenge: The client’s projects were plagued by poor quality assurance processes that resulted in high defect counts in production, stressful go-lives requiring emergency fixes, and extended post-implementation support. With no consistent testing methodology in place, quality standards varied widely between vendors and teams. This led to reduced user trust, higher rework costs, and unpredictable delivery timelines.
fields.cs_testimonial: “For the first time, go-live wasn’t a firefight. Maintain Technology’s assurance approach gave us the confidence that quality was baked in, not bolted on.”
fields.cs_why_it_matters: In complex IT programs, go-live quality is the difference between a smooth transition and a costly, reputation-damaging failure. Maintain Technology’s assured testing standards give leaders confidence that what’s going live is what was promised — working as intended, from day one.
fields.cs_approach_-_description_1: Maintain Technology implemented a testing assurance methodology to make quality a non-negotiable part of delivery:
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_1:
Reviewed past releases to identify defect trends, root causes, and test coverage gaps. 

Mapped testing practices across teams and vendors to understand inconsistencies.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_2:
Defined a standard test planning, execution, and acceptance process applicable across all projects. 

Embedded entry/exit criteria for every stage of testing (system, integration, UAT, regression).
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_3:
Introduced an independent QA oversight role to validate coverage, completeness, and traceability. 

Ensured test cases linked directly to business requirements and acceptance criteria.
fields.cs_approach_-_phase_description_4:
Shifted testing earlier in the cycle (“shift-left” approach). 

Introduced automated regression tests for high-risk areas.
fields.cs_result_-_list_1: Defects in production reduced by 65% compared to prior releases.
fields.cs_result_-_list_2: Zero critical defects at go-live for the first time in program history.
fields.cs_result_-_list_3: Stakeholder confidence increased — leadership had visibility of quality readiness before cutover.
fields.cs_result_-_list_4: Repeatable quality governance model implemented across future projects.
fields.cs_cta_-_title: Want Your Next Go-Live to Be a Non-Event? Let’s Talk.
fields.cs_cta_-_body_text: If your team is firefighting bugs post-release or dreading every cutover, we can help you bring calm, clarity, and confidence to your QA approach.

fields.cs_title: Rescued $500k in Avoidable ERP Cost Through Fast Assurance-Led Intervention
fields.cs_content: How Maintain Technology Helped Restore Delivery Confidence by Making Critical Decisions Before More Value Was Lost
fields.cs_outcome: Avoidable cost removed, decision-making restored, and delivery confidence strengthened.
fields.cs_subtitle: In a live ERP environment, three key decisions made within a few hours prevented $500k in unnecessary cost. The real issue was not the saving itself. It was that the cost should never have existed in the first place. Delivery had started to drift, accountability was diffused, and unresolved decisions were becoming expensive.
fields.cs_challenge: The program was not short on activity. It was short on clarity. Key decisions had been left sitting too long, ownership was blurred, and delivery risk was starting to convert into avoidable commercial impact. What appeared manageable on paper was already showing the signs of a program moving from delivery into rescue.
fields.cs_testimonial:
“Maintain Technology provided the independent assurance and decisive guidance our program needed at a critical moment. They quickly identified the key decision points driving unnecessary cost and helped us restore clarity, accountability, and confidence across delivery. Their intervention prevented further commercial loss and strengthened our ability to execute with control.”
— Senior Delivery Leader, Global ERP Program
fields.cs_why_it_matters: ERP programs rarely fail because people are inactive. More often, they lose confidence because the wrong issues are tolerated for too long. Delayed decisions, weak accountability, and unresolved risk are not signs of normal complexity. They are early indicators that rescue may already be required.
